requirement.description: The HTTP/2 hook implementation in h2.py is incomplete. It creates records but doesn't properly integrate with HTTP/2 connection handlers to populate request/response data. The tests indicate that records are created but often have zero-length content or missing data, and some tests fail because records aren't populated at all (e.g., len(records) == 0).
requirement.contract: HTTP/2 hook must properly intercept and track HTTP/2 requests/responses to ensure that all data (URL, method, status code, headers, content) is correctly captured and stored in the HTTP records. The hook must integrate with HTTP/2 connection handlers to populate the request and response data appropriately.

requirement.description: The HTTP2Record class in recordhttp2.py is missing proper data population mechanisms. The receive_data/send_data methods are implemented but don't properly handle HTTP/2-specific data flow. The URL construction logic is insufficient for HTTP/2 requests.
requirement.contract: HTTP2Record must properly handle data flow for HTTP/2 connections by implementing effective receive_data and send_data methods that populate request/response data correctly. URL construction should properly handle HTTP/2 pseudo-headers (:authority, :path) to form complete URLs.

requirement.description: The HTTPX hook implementation in httpx.py is duplicated from h2.py and has the same issues. It creates records but doesn't properly populate them with HTTP/2 data.
requirement.contract: HTTPX hook must properly handle HTTP/2 requests/responses by integrating with HTTP/2 connection handlers to ensure all request/response data is captured correctly.

requirement.description: The records.py module has an issue with the add_new_record method where it doesn't properly create HTTP2Record instances when record_type="http2". This causes all HTTP2 requests to be treated as HTTP1 records.
requirement.contract: The add_new_record method in HTTPRecords must correctly instantiate HTTP2Record objects when record_type="http2" is specified, and should properly handle the HTTP2Record's specific properties (URL, method, status_code, etc.).

requirement.description: The HTTP/2 hook implementation is missing support for HTTP/2 connection event handlers that would populate the record data after the HTTP/2 connection is established. This leads to records being created but with incomplete data.
requirement.contract: The HTTP/2 hook must implement proper connection event handling that allows HTTP/2 connection handlers to access the created records and populate them with actual request/response data as the connection progresses.
